scoring_justification: Full recompute is infeasible because the agent does not submit raw SO-CASCI output. Scoring uses reference matching (value‑vs‑gold with tolerances) plus mandatory structural ordering rules and boolean truth checks.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold SOC values and structural rules for scoring the spin‑orbit coupling constants and preferred crossover conclusions.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from Fig. 4 and the accompanying text of the paper: SOC(1A''→13A'')=480, SOC(13A''→5A')=373, SOC(13A''→1A')=266, SOC(5A''→23A'')=271, SOC(5A''→13A'')=9, SOC(23A''→1A')=796. The paper concludes both forward and backward crossovers are preferred.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values were taken verbatim from the paper. Tolerances of ±50 cm⁻¹ ( ±20 for the smallest coupling ) were chosen to accommodate numerical differences between implementations while excluding random guesses.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: All values are explicitly reported numeric quantities in the source paper.

outputs.description: Spin-orbit coupling constants for the six key state pairs governing forward and backward spin-crossover, plus boolean conclusions on pathway preference.

output_contract.notes: The agent must recompute SOC values via SO-CASCI. The hidden checker compares each reported SOC value to the paper's gold within a tolerance and checks that both boolean conclusions are true.

steps.description: Validate SOC values against paper gold within tolerance, enforce structural ordering, and verify boolean conclusions.

soc_value_match.description: Each SOC value matches paper gold within the stated absolute tolerance.

ordering.description: Required ordering relations among the SOC values (consistent with the paper's mechanism).

booleans.description: Both forward_crossover_preferred and backward_crossover_preferred must be true.
